summary: A semantic data table for comparing records: sortable columns, selectable rows, density-aware rows, and a focusable scroll region on narrow screens.
whenToUse: Records with the same attributes that users compare, sort or act on: tokens, components, pull requests.
Sortable headers (sortDirection + onSort, or useTableSort) on columns users reorder by.
Selectable rows: a Checkbox in the first cell, selected on the row, bulk actions above the table.
Compact density for expert, data-heavy screens.

Column widths when one column should not take the space of the others: width on the header cell, as a token length (var(--size-20)), a percentage or a fraction (0.35), plus minWidth for a floor. layout fixed keeps them exact while data loads.

narrowLayout stack when people read the table on a phone: under about 480px each row becomes a card, every value under its column name. Keep scroll (the default) for wide data people compare across rows.
whenNotToUse: Layout: never use a table to position content.
Fewer than three attributes per item: use a list.
Editing many cells inline like a spreadsheet: that needs a grid pattern, not in the system yet.

dos.title: Right-align numbers
dos.text: numeric aligns digits on the right with tabular figures, so values compare at a glance.

dos.title: Say what to do when it is empty
dos.text: TableEmpty keeps the header in place and explains how rows will appear.

children: No pull requests yet. Changes you sync from Figma appear here.

donts.title: Color as the only row state
donts.text: A tinted row alone does not say selected. Pair it with a checked Checkbox.

accessibility: Native table, thead, th scope col and td: screen readers announce headers with each cell.
Sortable headers contain a button; the th gets aria-sort ascending or descending on the sorted column only.
Selected rows set aria-selected and use the selected surface plus a checked Checkbox (never color alone).
The scroll container is a labelled region with tabIndex 0, so keyboard users can scroll wide tables (named by the caption or aria-label).
Row height and cell padding follow density: 48/36px rows, both above the 24px target minimum for the controls inside.

Stacked rows keep their table roles (table, row, cell), so screen readers still read cell by cell; the column names shown before each value are the header texts. The header row is hidden while rows stack, so put sorting somewhere else on phones.
contentGuidelines: Column headers are short nouns in sentence case: "Token", "Owner", "Uses".
Units go in the header ("Size (px)") so cells hold only values.
Empty cells show "None" or "n/a", never blank.
